subject: pharmacology
title: Ester versus Amide, Sodium Channel Blockade, Adrenaline, Neuraxial Techniques and Lipid Rescue

steps.tx: One benzene ring, one intermediate chain, one amine: local anaesthetics differ by the chain's link, **ester or amide**, and that bond decides metabolism and allergy. Esters (procaine, chloroprocaine, cocaine, tetracaine; one i in the generic name's older convention) are hydrolysed in plasma to PABA allergens. Amides (lignocaine, bupivacaine, ropivacaine, prilocaine; two i's) are hepatic, longer lived, and almost never truly allergenic. The spelling mnemonic survives because it works.
steps.say: One i, ester and plasma; two i's, amide and liver. The bond writes the biography.

left.title: Esters
points: Procaine, chloroprocaine, cocaine, benzocaine, tetracaine
Plasma cholinesterase hydrolysis, short action
PABA metabolite: the allergy family
Atypical cholinesterase prolongs their action

right.title: Amides
points: Lignocaine, bupivacaine, ropivacaine, prilocaine, mepivacaine
Hepatic metabolism, longer action
True allergy rare; preservatives usually blamed
Accumulate in liver failure and low output states

steps.tx: **Sodium channel blockade** is use dependent: the drug crosses the membrane uncharged, protonates inside, and binds the channel's inner pore preferentially when it is open or inactivated, so rapidly firing pain fibres accumulate block faster than quiet fibres. Small myelinated A delta and unmyelinated C pain fibres succumb before touch and motor fibres, producing the ordered loss: pain, temperature, touch, proprioception, motor. Acidosis in infected tissue ionises drug outside cells and defeats the block, which is why abscesses resist infiltration.
steps.say: Firing fibres block first and pain leaves first; acid tissue traps the drug outside and defeats it.

nodes.label: Uncharged drug crosses the nerve membrane
Protonated form binds inner sodium channel pore
Open and inactivated channels bind best: use dependence
Pain, temperature, touch, then motor function lost

steps.tx: **Adrenaline with local anaesthetic** constricts vessels at the injection site, slowing vascular uptake so the block lasts 30 to 50 percent longer, peak plasma levels fall, and the surgical field bleeds less; its tachycardia also betrays accidental intravascular test doses in epidural practice. Concentrations of 1:200,000 (5 microgram per ml) are typical. End arterial territories, digits, penis, ears and nose in compromised circulation, forbid or caution its use lest vasoconstriction ischaemically amputate what the block was meant to serve.
steps.say: Adrenaline keeps the drug local and longer; keep it away from end arteries that have no collateral mercy.

left.title: Adrenaline gains
points: Duration extended by a third to a half
Peak plasma levels and toxicity risk fall
Drier surgical field
Intravascular test dose signal in epidurals

right.title: Adrenaline prohibitions
points: Digits, penis and end arterial territories traditionally
Compromised flaps and grafts
Uncontrolled thyrotoxicosis and phaeochromocytoma caution
Cocaine anaesthetised tissue: catecholamine synergy

steps.tx: **Spinal anaesthesia** injects a small dose into cerebrospinal fluid at lumbar level for dense, rapid, reliable block below the chosen height: hyperbaric bupivacaine with glucose sinks under gravity to sculpt the level by positioning. Its signature complication is sympathetic blockade with hypotension and bradycardia, managed with fluids and vasopressors, and post dural puncture headache from cerebrospinal fluid leak, prevented by fine pencil point needles and treated by epidural blood patch when conservative measures fail.
steps.say: A millilitre in the CSF blocks everything below it; pressure and headache are the prices to manage.

steps.tx: **Epidural** technique parks drug outside the dura where larger volumes bathe nerve roots segmentally, giving a band of analgesia that can be topped up through a catheter for days: labour analgesia, thoracic perioperative care and cancer pain are its empires. Onset is slower and patchier than spinal, motor block lighter at analgesic concentrations, and the catheter adds abscess, haematoma and migration risks that anticoagulation timing rules exist to police.
steps.say: Epidurals trade spinal speed for a catheter's endurance; anticoagulant timing guards the space it lives in.

left.title: Spinal profile
points: Small dose, onset in minutes, dense block
Single shot duration fixed by agent choice
Hypotension from sympathetic blockade prominent
Post dural puncture headache the signature late cost

right.title: Epidural profile
points: Larger dose, onset over 15 to 20 minutes, segmental band
Catheter permits days of titrated analgesia
Test dose detects intrathecal or intravascular placement
Haematoma and abscess risks govern anticoagulant windows

steps.tx: **Cardiotoxicity** is bupivacaine's dark signature because its high lipid solubility and slow dissociation from cardiac sodium channels, combined with potassium and calcium channel effects, produce arrhythmias and contractile collapse resistant to standard resuscitation. Pregnancy increases sensitivity, acidosis and hypoxia amplify binding, and prevention is pure technique: aspiration, incremental dosing, test doses, ultrasound visualisation and dose ceilings. Ropivacaine and levobupivacaine were engineered specifically to widen this margin.
steps.say: Bupivacaine grips the heart's channels and will not let go; technique is the only reliable prevention.

nodes.label: Slow dissociation from cardiac sodium channels
Lipid emulsion plus prolonged CPR offers recovery

steps.tx: Intravenous **lipid emulsion** (20 percent Intralipid) rescues local anaesthetic systemic toxicity by two mechanisms: a lipid sink that extracts lipophilic drug from plasma and tissues down its gradient, and direct cardiotonic and metabolic support to the poisoned myocardium. Dosing is a 1.5 ml per kg bolus with infusion, repeatable to a ceiling near 12 ml per kg, started early in cardiovascular collapse and continued through prolonged resuscitation while standard measures proceed around it.
steps.say: Lipid emulsion sponges the drug out of the heart and feeds it meanwhile; start it early, not as a eulogy.

left.title: Lipid rescue protocol
points: 20 percent lipid emulsion stocked wherever blocks happen
Bolus 1.5 ml per kg, then infusion 15 ml per kg per hour
Repeat bolus and double infusion if unstable
Continue CPR prolonged: recovery can take an hour

right.title: Around the lipid
points: Stop injecting, call for help, airway and 100 percent oxygen
Benzodiazepines for seizures; avoid propofol in collapse
Adrenaline in small doses; avoid vasopressin and calcium blockers
Consider cardiopulmonary bypass where available

steps.tx: **Additives** refine blocks beyond adrenaline: clonidine and dexmedetomidine prolong neuraxial and peripheral blocks through alpha 2 mechanisms, opioids in the epidural space synergise segmentally, bicarbonate alkalinisation speeds onset by raising the uncharged fraction, and dexamethasone perineurally extends peripheral blocks by hours through debated mechanisms. Each additive imports its own adverse signature, so the plain agent's dose ceiling arithmetic from the previous lesson never leaves the calculation.
steps.say: Additives tune duration and onset; none of them repeals the maximum dose arithmetic.

left.title: Common additives
points: Adrenaline: duration and intravascular signal
Clonidine or dexmedetomidine: prolongation, sedation cost
Bicarbonate: faster onset by alkalinisation
Dexamethasone perineural: hours of extension

right.title: Additive discipline
points: Preservative free preparations for neuraxial use
Each additive's adverse effects owned and monitored
Local anaesthetic ceiling dose unchanged
Evidence graded per block type, not assumed
